utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm sorry for the delay because I got confused with the courtroom. Yes, Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm sorry but I did forget to tender offer under evidence yesterday D61/3, which was the audiotape which was played in the courtroom. If it's not too late since there are no objections from the Prosecution, may I tender that exhibit for the Defence into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think at this stage I'll bear your request in mind, and we'll continue with the cross-examination of this witness. After this witness leaves the courtroom, we'll deal with it. It might need some discussion on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karnavas, are you ready to continue your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Good afternoon, good afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Karnavas [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to pick up where we left off yesterday. Now, since last -- now, since yesterday did you have an opportunity to go over your statement again last night after you left?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I take it you read it again?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And because -- I actually read it several times. And I was trying to remember details and everything. And I had problems because of your questioning and because of my memory, I tried to recall everything. But really --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness come closer to the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... Completely, you, yourself. And I came to the conclusion, and I apologise to everybody, to you, to the Presiding Judge, and to the Prosecutor, really. I cannot remember all the details, and I would not like to lay the blame on somebody. And I wouldn't like to do that because of me, through my own fault. Because really, I cannot remember the particulars, the details. I really couldn't tell you that, because it's been a long time since then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I take it that when you were in Banja Luka you had the same problem as well?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Though, in Banja Luka at times when you were answering questions, I take it, sometimes you were not quite sure whether you were being accurate or not?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told the investigative Judges also at the time. I really cannot -- you've read it, everybody's read it. I wasn't really able to recall the details, the precise details, how many people entered the bus or how many people left the bus, because really, I am not able to remember everything. Everything that I said and everything that I signed, I understand that I can be punished for all of that and I'm not trying to escape that. But really, last night -- even up to 5.00 this morning, I was leafing through it all. And perhaps I made a mistake with regard to certain people. Perhaps, I don't know, Mr. Blagojevic knew that I wasn't able -- that I couldn't be an officer on duty. I was possibly just able to check the civilian people entering the command or something like that. And I wasn't able to get in touch with anybody. And perhaps I made a mistake with regard to this Jovanovic. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you here for a second. First of all, let me just say that we want -- we would like you to be as accurate as you can, every one of us here. Secondly, you're not going to be punished -- or, you know, if you were confused or if you were mistaken. All right. Now, before I start my questioning, I just wanted to point out on the first page you indicate - and I read from page 1, line 18 to 19 in the English version - you say: "As I explained to you when I show you last time, you know, I worked as a driver just to provide to my family." Do you recall reading that? It's on the first page of the statement.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, my question is: Did you meet with the Office of the Prosecution before on another occasion, or was this the very first time you met with them in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 13th of October, that is the first time. And I think that's when Mr. Bursik was there and Peter -- this gentleman right here. I don't know. He was there. I also came the first time, but there was a mistake in the translation of the summons because I -- in the version -- in the Serbian language, in the Serbo-Croatian language it said the 23rd of October, that's what the summons said. But in the English language version, it was the 13th of October. So I came because the summons in the Serbo-Croatian language was signed by -- at the ministry in Banja Luka that was in charge of all of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is: Were you questioned once or were you questioned more than one time?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, I'm going to need shorter answers, if possible. I'm going to try to ask very direct questions so we can get you back home?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. No problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know Mr. Mirko Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you know him -- do you know him well?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got to know him better only after 1994 when I became a member of the military police. Before that, I just knew him by sight because he worked in Tuzla as a driver in Trans Service. That was the company in Tuzla. That was the name of it at the time. Now it's called Trans Tuzla. But before that until September, we didn't have any contacts. We didn't really socialise. Only when I got to the military police, then we officially met one another and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did you have a good working relationship with him?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had business relations. The things that I had to do, the things that Jankovic and Jovanovic and the Bratunac security officer, Mr. Nikolic, that's the things that they told me to do, I would carry them out. Before that, I was at the checkpoint towards the border with Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I don't want to interrupt you, but are you telling us that you had a good working relationship, a professional relationship, with him?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you know a Mile Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was also a member of the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that at the time back in July - 11th, 12th and so on, of 1995 - Mile Petrovic was actually the deputy commander? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as you sit here today, you're still under the impression that Jovanovic was the commander and Jankovic was the deputy commander?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came to the military police in September, then I was told that Jankovic was -- that's when I met Jankovic -- actually Jovanovic, that they were the commander and the deputy commander. And afterwards, what the structural changes were in the command or by their duties, I really don't know. I didn't have the right to know who appointed whom or anything like that. And like I said yesterday, I --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, we're talking about the commander of the military police and the deputy commander. So if the commander --

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- wasn't around, you would be receiving your orders from the deputy commander; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So if Mile Petrovic was the deputy commander, you might have received some orders from him? Is that possible or is it your recollection that you never received any orders from him, which may be a possibility as well?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The premises of the military police were the place where most of us actually spent time. There was some people who were older than myself. They were between 35 and 40 years old at the time. So if Jovanovic or Jankovic weren't there -- one of them was usually with us, either Jovanovic. But if none of them were there, then they always said to one of the older people to be the person in charge, to be on duty in case people needed to be brought in, like the conscripts who would just leave the lines without permission and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, we're going to focus now on the period of around July 11th to the 16th, 17th, during that period of time, okay, 1995. This is right around the fall of Srebrenica. Okay?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I take it from listening to your answers, as you stand here today you're not sure who was your deputy commander during that period?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, in your statement you indicated when you were asked about who told you to go to Potocari, you indicated - and I'm quoting from, it's in the English version, page 6, line 17 - you think -- "I think that Mirko Jankovic approached me."

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you recall whether or not he, in fact, approached you or were you just saying that in Banja Luka because that's -- you assumed that that's what happened?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are a couple of us sitting there and he said, You have to go up there. We assumed because there were these families who were victims for -- during Christmas 1995 -- 1993. Then there were about 50 families at Zalas [phoen] also who were victims for St. Peter's Day. They perished in 1992. So this is what we were most afraid of at that point in time. So we were really trying to try to protect --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, I'm going to ask you to please listen to the questions and just answer the questions, okay, not what's in the statement. My question to you is: Did Mirko Jankovic, in fact --

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- in fact approach you or was that an assumption you were making in Banja Luka at the time that you were giving your statement? Which of the two? And if you're not sure, just say I'm not sure. That's another possibility.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do not want to say anything bad or to liable anybody with the things that I say, but I don't know. This is what I said, so I cannot go back on what I said. But as far as I can see, I think that he did come up to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So again, I cannot ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now -- and according to you, you were at the police station -- at the military police compound when he came up to you? That's your testimony?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, you were here when they played the tape yesterday. I went to Potocari of my own free will. There are some others there --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that --

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My colleagues who were also members of the military police at the time, together with me. But according to that statement and to my statement, it seems that I went just of my own volition, that -- and all the others, that they went there just like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you one of them?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was at the beginning. Later, they returned -- they told me to leave. And that's when I was next -- I went to be by the buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So initially you were sent to Potocari along with other members of the Bratunac Brigade military police to provide security for General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was security for General Mladic, that was only in front of the Hotel Fontana, where he was having, I think, talks with the commander of the Dutch Battalion that was in Srebrenica. There I was securing the hotel, and after that - as I said a moment ago - six or seven of us sat in a military vehicle and we went in the direction of Potocari. And then I followed them up there to the security point to secure the convoys, the boarding of the buses, and all that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm trying to get a clear answer from you, Mr. Zaric. Were you selected, were you selected, to provide security for General Mladic, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did -- is it possible that Mr. Jovanovic sent you there, since you think he was still over there?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said a while ago, at the beginning before I started making the statement, really after this night that I didn't sleep at all, I tried hard to recall whether he was or not -- and I'm not sure and I cannot claim with certainty whether he was or not. In fact, I am self-conscious, actually. I'm having a hard time. I don't want to incriminate anybody by my statement. I don't want anyone to have consequences on that account. As I say, I read everything about the Tribunal and what awaits me from the Tribunal if I make a wrong statement and I'm clear on that. But I really would not like to burden anyone by any statement of mine. Because ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, when you were meeting with the Prosecution in Banja Luka, did they question you first or did they show you the video first and then ask you questions or was it during the interviewing process? Which of the three?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They started showing it during the talk, the interview.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, first I started with this, that you have at the beginning. And then they started showing what have you -- the actual date when the footage started running, the time, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's when you saw yourself?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So my question again is: Is it possible, sir, that you were there to provide security for General Mladic; and once you got there, you were tasked by someone to go to the bus, where you were located on the video?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps. I cannot recall with precision because I didn't go with that group in the vehicle. I only went up there later because I think that it was a Pitzgauer military vehicle, so some six or seven of them went on it. And I was driven up there subsequently. And when I got up there, they told me, You are to secure the command -- nobody told me, nobody told me that you are going to secure the commander of the Army of Republika Srpska, General Mladic, but they just told me you have to go there as secure. So another four or five men came with me. I cannot recall all the names. When we got there, this man - I believe it is the one -- the guy who is standing by me on the videoclip. He told me, you stand here by me and we'll let these people through to go to the bus. This is the order that I got from him. And from whom he got that order, I don't know. And then I went back to Potocari later. As I said, I was just securing the area in front of the Fontana.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We're going to go step by step. So if I understand you correctly, you were never directly sent to Potocari to provide security for the Muslim refugees; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They just told me, Go up there to secure the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And once you got there, someone told you to stand by the bus?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This colleague who was with me, he told me. He was on the photograph, on the footage with me, because he happened to be there near the bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you say "colleague," is he someone from the Bratunac Brigade military police or is he just a colleague because he's a VRS soldier?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this guy who is in the photograph with me who was shown yesterday standing by me, next to the bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, who --

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were some sort of friends, let me not go into that, to explain --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But my question is very direct. Is he another member of the Bratunac Brigade military police? Is he from the Bratunac Brigade? Or is he from some other unit that you don't know? Those are the three choices.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is from the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, did he tell you where he got his orders from?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you did not -- so it wasn't Mirko Jankovic giving you any orders to go by the buses; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you certainly didn't see your commander, Colonel Blagojevic, there that day?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday I said that it was only after all this, it was the 14th or the 15th in the evening, that I learned that Mr. Blagojevic was the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, because -- well, I know, I know, Mr. Blagojevic from the time I was a child. And we come from the same place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is, sir: You did not see him there, and that's what you told to the folks in Banja Luka; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I didn't see him at Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. That's what -- we're talking about Potocari now. Now, you indicated that you saw some other members -- well, staying with the military police, during your interview you said that -- you were asked -- and this is at the bottom of page 6, line 25: "And when you were deployed to the enclave, who was deployed with you?" And your answer was, page 7, line 1 in the English version: "So all of us, everybody in the military police. I think about 20 of us, well, were all deployed in that area." And then you're asked: "And was there -- were you all summoned to one central point before being deployed and given briefing?" And the answer is: "No." Mr. Zaric, are you certain about this aspect of your statement, that about 20 of you were sent to Potocari on that particular day, keeping in mind that Bratunac had approximately 30 military police officers at any given time?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said about 20, and earlier there were six or seven. I cannot say exactly how many there were who were escorting General Mladic. After us, some four or five or so arrived. I cannot say exactly how many. So I said that there were some 20-odd. Whether it was exactly 20 or less, I can't say. I don't even know how many of us there were on the military police force there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So am I correct in concluding that when you said: "I think about 20 of us," you were just guessing?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it could be fewer than ten?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There could have been.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There could have been as few as five or six, the ones that you saw?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well maybe, because I don't know where those who were escorting General Mladic were at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you got to Potocari on that day, you also noticed - as you did on the film - that there were other soldiers from some battalions of the Bratunac Brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it, because they were there on the video standing there on the side of the road, as we saw them, you assumed that they had been ordered to be there; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that they were ordered to be there in order to guard the Muslim population that was there; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had no contact at all with them. They were not members of the military police. They were under the battalion command. Now, whether they were from the 1st or the 2nd or the 3rd Battalion, I didn't know that. Some of those whom I saw on the footage I recognised and I said who they were, because I had been with them, as they say, until yesterday. Before I joined the military police, I was on the same line with them up to that point. And perhaps had I remained in the battalion that they were members of, I would have perhaps been standing by the road just like them, had I not joined the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But my question, sir, is -- well, let's go step by step. When you were in Potocari on the 12th, you never went up there to them or to speak to your fellow soldiers; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember now whether I did go or not. If I did approach someone, it was just to say hello or something like that but not really to talk about what they were doing or how they were doing it. I cannot say exactly whether I did or not. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you didn't see that in your statement anywhere, did you, when you were reading your statement, that you had actually gone and met with your fellow soldiers and had any discussions with them? It's not in your statement, is it?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it is said at a certain point in the statement -- it is written that that morning or the next day, I cannot the date until I have a look at it, they were securing the area around because in the SFOR base --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're going to get to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President, if the witness could just finish his sentence he was about to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's okay, Your Honour. I'm trying to speed things up, but we have all day tomorrow as well as I understand it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go on and finish your sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, you may finish your sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey can object as well, Your Honour. I have no objections to both of them objecting or the gentleman from the back.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe, as I said a while ago, I may have got in touch with - and I don't know what the exact date is until I leaf through this - those people who were securing behind the base, SFOR, and behind the Dutch base there, that is the only time I established contact with them, some of them were familiar. Otherwise, with the other ones I didn't like to get in touch, in fact, nor did I. And to this day, as they say, I -- apart from the fact that I've come here to testify, I don't like to talk about it at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we need to talk about the details. Now, in your statement there's nowhere where you state that you went and you spoke to these soldiers and that you learned what, if any, assignments they had in Potocari on the 12th; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's not correct? In your statement, when in Banja Luka, you never told the officers there, the investigators, that you had spoken to any of those soldiers; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said a while ago, I may have stated that I talked, but I don't know what the date was exactly until I leaf through it to see. But as far as I can recall, I did not talk to anyone on the 12th. It may have been the 13th or the 14th, I really don't know. But I think, as far as I can recall, on the 12th I didn't talk to anyone there. I may have approached a person or two, you know, to light my cigarette or something like that, but I didn't talk to anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked on page 8, and I'm reading from line 9, that's in the English version: "Who else was there when you arrived?" And your answer is: "I cannot tell you exactly which units were there. They all had camouflage uniforms on, so I was not able because we were all -- we all wore the same camouflage uniforms and they had no signs. So I was not able to determine whether someone was police or some special unit or something." That would be on page 8, line 10 in the Srpski version. You're then asked, if you could -- it's page 8, line 10, that's what I read.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I take it, had you gone up to some of those soldiers and had a conversation with them, you might have asked them from which unit they were from; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you're telling us here that you don't know which units they were from; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you're asked later on: "But you were in the military and this is your area of responsibility. How could you have not known who these people are? There are troops, civilians, and yet there's all these armed people standing around." And your answer is: "So I was told to go there and I was also told there would be some people from the battalion, and I was told to go there near the UN base and secure that area. "My question to you, sir, is: Who told you that people from the battalion would be there?" Or was this just something you were assuming when you were giving your statement, because you saw some of your fellow soldiers there on the video?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible that nobody told you and you just saw that on the video and you assumed?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After a group of buses had left with women and children aboard and the rest, I went behind, I believe, the technical repairs shop of Crvenka transport into a woods there. I cannot recall exactly who came and said that there was no one securing the area there and that we had to go to the transport firm in Srebrenica -- in Potocari, because there at the entrance were many people so that we had to see that that was handled. I cannot remember who came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Were you just assuming that, because there were soldiers there and you had seen some from the Bratunac Brigade, that all those soldiers were from the Bratunac? Was that just an assumption that you were making?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew some of them, as I said awhile ago, and I had known some of them prior to joining the military police because I would be occasionally assigned to help in the other battalions. So I cannot say exactly this is that person, this is so-and-so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, is it an assumption on your part that since there were members of the Bratunac Brigade there, that they had to be an assignment?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most probably they were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Because that would seem natural; correct? So you don't know whether some just left the line and out of curiosity went to Bratunac, or whether in fact they were given orders by their commanders to go there?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Isn't it just as likely, isn't it just as likely, that those men may have gone there to Potocari out of curiosity and never had any orders? Isn't that just as likely of a possibility?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a possibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of the people that you notice in the film was a soldier from the Bratunac Brigade who was quite often on the list for the military police to locate and arrest. Do you recall that person?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I think he goes by the nickname of Like?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as I understand it from your testimony, he was sort of a free spirit, an independent person, who never liked to be under command; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To tell you the truth, he would try to play the macho guy. I don't know how old he was, but he wasn't married or anything like that. So he liked to -- but I don't know which battalion he was a member of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But my point is --

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My point is: Here is one individual who was quite often on the list for leaving the line and doing whatever he wanted to do; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the people that you saw on the video who are on the side - I believe it would be on the left side as the car is driving down - they're just standing there or walking by; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some were standing, some were walking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And again, just by looking at that video and by looking at what those soldiers were doing at the time, you cannot tell us with any degree of certainty that they weren't there just out of curiosity and walking through or that they actually had been sent there by their commanders to carry out a particular order?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that a little bit earlier, that I really -- I just perhaps went up to them to ask them for a light for my cigarette or something like that. I didn't ask them anything. I didn't ask them why they were standing there or anything like that. I was standing over there where the people were entering the buses. So I really had no intention of creating any kind of excess or, I don't know, outburst. I am the kind of person who wouldn't like to ruin somebody else by my actions or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we appreciate that. We just want you to tell us to the best of your recollection what it is that you remember. Now, the following day -- are you okay?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm a little tired because I didn't sleep, but no problem. I will try to go on as long as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the following day - now we're talking about the 13th of July, okay?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what I've read in your statement, you go to the compound where the military police are stationed in Bratunac around 11.00 to 12.00; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're just sitting around with your colleagues drinking coffee, waiting for some order?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at some point you're asked to go back to Potocari; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in your statement you say that Dragisa Jovanovic was present there on that morning; correct? It's on page -- if you just want to look at it, I can focus you on the right page. It's on page 18 of the English version, line 2. It should be around page 17 --

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember, because I leafed through this many times last night and I read it. And as I said at the beginning of this testimony today, last night and after the conversation with you yesterday and the cross-examination, I really apologise to the gentlemen, to the Judges, to the Prosecution, and to you, and also to the gentlemen Jokic and Blagojevic over there. I -- when I try to remember something -- I don't know, maybe Jovanovic wasn't in Bratunac. I really cannot claim whether he was or wasn't, so I am unsure about that. I've said many times already, if I need to be held accountable for that statement, then very well, I can be held accountable for it. But I thought about that statement so much and everything that I was up all night. I didn't sleep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it's possible that you just made a mistake, that you just got mixed up on the dates; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I mixed up the dates. Maybe I said it wrongly, that he was there. But I really do not wish to liable anyone or blacken anybody's name. I really --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're not suggesting you're doing that. We're just trying to see if we can get you to recall the events. Okay. So don't worry about what you said, we're just trying to have you now help us out with some details. Okay. But if Mr. -- Now, if Mr. Jovanovic states, as he did to the Office of the Prosecution back on 26th November 2001 in his statement, and it's on page 9. He states that -- he's asked when did he leave Bratunac. And he states that: "It was on the 18th or 19th of June." You would have no reason to distrust him, would you?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I would not. I really wouldn't like anything like that. That's why last night I looked over this a thousand and one times and read it back. And I really didn't -- I had some sort of inner unrest and I just couldn't -- but I really wouldn't like to wrongly accuse anyone or anything like that. Because -- well, perhaps as they say, we're all responsible for there and ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the 13th at some point you indicated you went to Potocari; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in your statement you indicate that you went there sometime -- or first you say: "Maybe around 1400 hours," that would be about 2.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I really cannot remember the precise details, whether I came at 11.00 or not. Maybe I came at 10.00. Or if I did come, it was maybe around or close to noon. So I really cannot tell you when I went up there what time it was and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you state that when you went to Potocari you went there with the TAM truck?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you were asked if Mirko Jankovic was with you at the time, and you indicated: "Yes." My question is: Are you sure or were you just assuming that he must have been with you; which of the two?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, this was on the 13th, we entered the base. I don't know exactly. I cannot remember because I don't know whether it was on the 13th or -- I can't remember exactly. They allowed us in because of the buses, because there were a lot of people who had entered the SFOR base in Potocari. So they allowed us to come in with the buses. They allowed the buses in so that we would escort them -- I don't know whether they went towards Kladanj or -- I don't know about that. But we went in together with the soldiers of the international forces, they were standing together with us, the ones who were still there in Potocari. So as far as I can recall, Jankovic didn't stay there for very long. Maybe he came with us and then the TAMic returned immediately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, are you sure he came with me or are you just assuming he came with you? If you don't know --

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he came after us. I think that he came after us, but I cannot be sure. I think I might have seen him for a moment, but again, I cannot be sure. I really would not like to ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were also asked if you saw Momir Nikolic on the 13th. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you had seen him on the 12th; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from reading your statement, I didn't see anywhere where you noticed him coordinating the various units that were there or giving orders to superior officers on how the evacuations should take place?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I couldn't have been present there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he had -- well, he was my teacher in secondary school, and we were on friendly terms. But we were aware of his rank and my rank, and perhaps I could have just gone up to say hello to him and leave. But I wasn't really meant to stand there and stay there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Are we going to go beyond, Your Honour, because we started a little bit late?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, perhaps we could make a stop here and we could resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, would you please tell me how much time you still need for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Hopefully I can wrap it up, Your Honour, within about 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, when we left off we were speaking about Mr. Nikolic on the -- on July 13th. Okay?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, from your statement you indicate that you did see Mr. Nikolic, Momir Nikolic, in Potocari on the 13th when you went there. Do you recall reading that in your statement?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you also recall reading in your statement that it was your recollection that a conversation took place between Mirko Jankovic and Momir Nikolic? Do you recall reading that? For the record, I'm referring to page 22, and it's between the lines 8 and --

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall reading that? Now, you indicated that you overheard a conversation between Mirko Jankovic and Momir Nikolic; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you sit here today, are you certain that this conversation ever took place on July 13th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say whether that was on the 13th of July, 1995, or whether it was on the 12th or the 14th, but I think that it did happen. I cannot say that with certainty, but I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you think there was a conversation at some point in time between Mirko Jankovic and Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall -- and would that have been in Potocari or could that have been in Bratunac? Could it have been some other place?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in your statement, you state that it was the 13th; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you state that it took place sometime around 1500, 1600, or 1700 hours - again for the record that's on page 22, line 22, 21 and 22 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what if I were to tell you, Mr. Zaric, that on the 13th of July Mr. Nikolic has testified that he was only in Potocari for an hour or so early in the morning sometime around 10.00 to 11.00 that morning, and that after that he left? Would you tend to believe Mr. Nikolic or would you tend to believe your memory?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly at the moment what date it was. It's been a long time since then, and things have happened. So I don't know whether this was on the 12th in the afternoon or on the 13th. I really cannot remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it would not come to you as a surprise if you were to learn, then, that according to Momir Nikolic, during that period of time he was at or around the vicinity of Konjevic Polje on that road someplace at the same time that you stated, in Banja Luka, he was in Potocari having a conversation with Mirko Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well -- and if that is possible and if Mr. Jankovic were to also state that earlier in the day he was with, he was with Momir Nikolic and Mile Petrovic, during that period of time when you would have thought to have seen Momir Nikolic or Mile Petrovic in Potocari, you would have no reason today to disbelieve them, would you?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The two of them kept their own records of where they went, so I don't know. As far as I'm concerned, I don't know whether it was on the 12th or on the 13th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I said the wrong date or something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, because the dates are very critical in this case. That's the only reason why we're going over this. And on that particular day we know that sometime in the early afternoon, at least from the testimony that has come before this Tribunal, that Nikolic, Jankovic, and Petrovic were together on that stretch of road leading towards Konjevic Polje and were not in that other direction in Potocari, where you might have been?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, yesterday and today we discussed several areas where you have acknowledged that you've been incorrect with your facts, as you stated them in Banja Luka, facts such as who was your commander; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were wrong about that?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were wrong about who was your deputy commander; correct? Or you still don't know?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, may I just say what I've already repeated many times. I came to the military police in September. The commander was Dragisa Jovanovic, and his deputy was Mirko Jankovic. So after that what changed or -- we had no idea about that. We didn't know who appointed them or anything like that. And I wasn't interested either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me quote to you from a statement given by Mr. Jankovic on 28 November 2001, where he says on page 10, he says -- and I'm reading from line 1: "Then next is my deputy, and my deputy was Mile Petrovic." And he goes on to state on page -- on the same page, lines 3 and 4 -- 3 to 5 that: "He was appointed to that post by the command because he was a good man, honest, and conscientious and so on." This is a statement given by Mirko Jankovic to the Prosecution. Now, as you stand here today, you have no reason to disbelieve Mr. Jankovic, do you?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So just to recap, so that was one more example of you being wrong, not knowing who indeed was your deputy commander at the time when Srebrenica fell; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were also not sure -- or you were also wrong with respect to Jovanovic; correct, Mr. Jovanovic being in Potocari, you were wrong on that instance as well. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Just in terms of clarification, the witness said what he believed was correct at the time he gave the statement in Banja Luka or today. That doesn't necessarily mean it's wrong what he's saying. If counsel puts his information to him, that's his side, but I think it's misleading if we put something to a witness saying, you know, this is right or wrong. I think he has testified to his personal observations and he has given the basis for these observations. If he believes at a certain time that a certain person was his commander or his deputy commander, then that's his belief. He can be cross-examined what the basis is for that belief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Karnavas, in the past you always distinguish the different characteristics of the questions, whether his statement is wrong or whether the facts is another matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I totally agree with you, Your Honour, but if I may, and I don't want to have a long debate, but I'm sure the Prosecution knows that I have a good-faith basis for making these statements and eliciting from the witness his confession of error. But I will, because they know from their own documentation who was the commander or the deputy commander and where was Mr. Jovanovic at the time, these are facts that are well within their grasp and reach and not something I am making up as a result of my own investigation. Be that as it may, I will proceed in another direction and I will be wrapping up my cross, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: By the way, Mr. Karnavas, I believe those questions have been asked and answered during your cross-examination already. There's no need to sum up for us, if I may say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, as you aptly pointed out, Mr. President, there was a slight different spin to the line of questioning, but if I may have the indulgence in perhaps one or two questions, then -- and I will sit down. But I see the point. Incidentally, just for the record, I'm reminded when I'm making a reference to Mr. Jankovic's statement for identification purposes is D53/1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, during the period that we've had to discuss your statement, it's fairly clear that as you sit here today you're rather confused as to the dates, the places, the names, and the events; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it when you were back in Banja Luka, you were equally confused, though you were trying to do the best that you could, given the fact that the events took place several years earlier; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you knew you were being questioned as a suspect; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were, as I understand it from reading your statement, rather concerned as to what might happen, because back home in Potocari you were concerned for your child because of an incident that had occurred, a tragic incident that had occurred, in your family. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I think that I will have about half an hour's worth of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may proceed. Cross-examined by Mr. Stojanovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Zaric.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will try to concentrate on the part relating to the 14th and the Zvornik Brigade. And since we are speaking the same language, could you please make sure that you don't start answering right away, but only when you get the signal then to start so that the interpreters can do their job as well.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you several questions which are directly related to your testimony of yesterday. When I was preparing for this cross-examination and reading your statement, I came to a part which was interpreted differently yesterday and I wanted to clarify that. In the statement that you gave to the Prosecution in Banja Luka, the question about the 14th and the arrival to the Zvornik Brigade was whether Mirko Jankovic was with you, and you said no. And then there was a question whether Dragisa Jovanovic was with you and you said yes. These questions were put by Mr. McCloskey. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was going over that last night, so perhaps you mentioned that many times. In the course of the questioning today, I'm uncertain mostly and I was suffering because of that myself and agonising over it until dawn because I was not able to tell things precisely. A long time has passed since then and everything. So I cannot say exactly about Dragisa Jovanovic. I'm not sure about the statement that I gave to the investigative organs there and so on. I am not trying to evade the consequences. And if I have to be accountable for the things I have said, I will, and that's it. I really cannot commit liable about somebody if I'm not sure whether they were there or not. And I would definitely not like to do something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that, and it is quite clear in view of the passage of time that we can have this misunderstanding. But I understood yesterday's testimony and today's testimony in the sense that you still think that it is possible that Mr. Dragisa Jovanovic was not there?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I apologise for this, because, for example, when I was shown my statement from Banja Luka, I could have said this then. But even then I wasn't sure and I'm not sure now. So I am saying openly that I am not sure about that answer of mine and all that. Really, that is how I feel now. I really would not like to sully anyone's name if I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is exactly why, Radenko, I would like to ask you whether it's possible that you perhaps switched names and that Mirko Jankovic went with you in that column of buses which went towards Zvornik on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it was Mirko Jankovic either, really. A person cannot be sure. I'm trying to remember everything, but really, I cannot remember the details. But I believe that Mirko wasn't there either or Dragisa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the next question would be how many of you accompanied the buses and was anybody in charge of that group that was accompanying the buses?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was alone in the bus. There were women and children in the buses, and there were elderly men. There were also some younger ones and so on. But I was alone in the bus. And we perhaps boarded not more than 40 people per bus. There were attempts by those who had acquaintances. They asked not to be separated. If there were families, they asked not to be separated into different buses, because I was hearing stories that some people were being sent towards Vlasenica, Sekovici, and Kladanj and some of the other buses were sent towards Zvornik and so on. In front of us there was a military vehicle. It was the corps military police that was at the head of the column. I don't know whether it was a Pitzgauer or some other vehicle. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was there also security in the other vehicles, or were you the only security staff in the whole column, other than those who were in the Pitzgauer or in the other military vehicle?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were also military security people in the other buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall the names of any other people who were with you escorting the column?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who else was there. Where I was going, I think there were some people from the corps police. There were a couple of men from the Zvornik military police, but I'm not sure whether they were members of the Zvornik military police or not. But I saw them when they were standing there around the Zvornik Brigade command. I could tell that they knew the people who were at the entrance, at the gate, and so on. So I cannot say exactly whether they were members of the Zvornik Brigade military police or not, but there were people there from the corps military police. So I don't know whether there were others who were accompanying the convoy. I cannot remember that now, because down there where I went, I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Radenko, does that mean that only you were in the convoy from the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps there were others also, but I cannot remember that now. I'm trying, and I'm burdening myself with it. But I'm trying as much as possible to recall, but I cannot remember. At the time, I didn't see anybody. I don't know whether some people went before me or after me, but I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me say that I was not in that group. I was in the bus which was painted in military colours. It was -- if you're from our area you would know that the buses were -- had the insignia "VRS." And I was in that bus. There was a hold-up, and somebody said that there was a possibility that the bus needed to be emptied and that there would be another bus, and that I would have to drive the people towards Baljkovica because the Muslims who were trying to break out of Srebrenica towards Tuzla - this is the conversation that I heard - had committed a massacre near Baljkovica and this person told my driver that about 40 people were killed on that occasion and that people had to be driven up there in order to help out. So at that point I left the bus because I was afraid that they would also transfer me up there in that direction. So I tried to go towards Konjevic Polje. And at that point, from the brigade, I can't remember because I didn't really talk to that man very much, a vehicle came out. I stopped the vehicle, and it took me up to Drinjaca, somewhere around there. And from there, I slowly went on foot. The vehicle went to Zelen Polje [phoen] or something, I don't know exactly. So I slowly walked towards Konjevic Polje. And a military vehicle caught up with me, so then I was taken all the way up to Konjevic Polje; that's where the checkpoint was. The civilian police had already set up a checkpoint, so there were a lot of people there. I could see there was some soldiers were milling around, and I asked a civilian police officer if I can be taken to Bratunac. So the first vehicle that came along took me to Bratunac, but I cannot remember who was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we have a situation here that we need to clarify. We have information here about the fighting at Baljkovica and we have information about the number of killed. You're talking about the 14th. These battles and the people who were killed were not -- that did not happen on the 14th. So the question is: Is it possible that this event that you're talking about was not on the 14th but maybe on the 15th?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's possible. I cannot say that exactly. I've said that before. Perhaps I've mistaken about the dates here as well, because when the other gentleman, the other lawyer, was questioning me, I said that. So it's possible. I really am not able to remember the precise dates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But can we agree that this -- that you came after you received or heard the information about the 40 fighters killed in the area of Baljkovica you arrived in the escort of this convoy?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that in Zvornik in front of the command because we were held up. The buses were just standing there. I don't know. I could not say there were 50 buses that had stopped there, but I'm not sure because I didn't know the exact number because I wasn't interested in that. But a man came up to me. He left the gate, approached the driver. I don't know whether they knew each other or not. He just said there was the possibility that-- he probably did know him. So I cannot say exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it is possible that this did not take place on the 14th, and you are quite certain that it was after you received information about some 40 killed fighters?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that information when it was told me by this person. I was sitting there by the driver, at the conductor's seat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we agree that this had to have taken place after these people were killed?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you cannot say what date it was?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zaric. There is another thing I wish to clarify. You said that there was a bus with marks of the Army of the Republika Srpska. That was the licence plate's marks. So when you said they had this mark, were you referring to the licence plates or to the sides of the bus? And was this on one bus or on all the buses in the convoy?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was on quite a few buses. I was in Potocari. There were buses of the Army of Republika Srpska that didn't have any markings on their sides. For instance, Vihor or Drina Trans or Central Trans was -- or any transport firm on the bus. They had just on their licence plates demark VRS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these marks were on all the buses, were they not?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were not on all the buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this convoy?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were also buses with civilian licence plates there, because this was an organised transport. Because of the load of the -- that the buses had to take up there in the fields near Glogova, if you know where that is, one of the older buses, because it was overloaded, actually came on fire. Actually the clutch plate broke down and it couldn't actually make it up the hill so that -- they told us that thereafter we could only have up to 40 -- between 30 and 40 people aboard the bus. That is why we stopped there, because we wanted to prevent the buses from being overloaded and wanted to avoid any problems and wanted to avoid any protests by the people because of the way their families were being treated in the bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many buses in all were on the convoy, and were there only buses in it or trucks as well?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you the exact number of the buses, and this is what I've also told the investigators. They were directing in Konjevic Polje some of the buses towards Kladanj. Perhaps every second or third bus would be sent in the direction of Kladanj, and other buses again towards Zvornik. So this is the way they were sending them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I hate to interrupt, I'm told by my colleague --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I hate to interrupt here, but I'm told by my colleague that there may have been an error in the translation to the previous question with respect to the gentleman's answer as far as, you know, the answer dealing with the civilians in the buses and who they were trying to protect them from and the protests. I don't want to give the answer, what I believe it might be, but it's page 40, lines 5 to 7. So perhaps the answer could be asked again by Mr. Stojanovic and the gentleman could be given an opportunity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. Just one point of clarification, but I would need to go to private session for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Zaric, we'll go back to a segment of what you testified about here. Just let me wrap up this first part. Last time when you were answering the Prosecutor's questions - I'm referring to the statement in Banja Luka - you said that about four to five buses were there. Today you say that you do not remember. Can you tell us approximately what was the size of this convoy.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you about the exact quantity when we came down there, when this person said that we were supposed to go to Baljkovica. I went outside and we stood there and there were about four or five buses there. And then more buses arrived afterwards, but I cannot tell you exactly from where they came. I don't know and I wasn't interested. And then I boarded the bus again. And I only managed to ask, Am I still needed here? Then they told me, Somebody will be coming shortly to see about the buses. Then a man came who I cannot describe exactly, nor do I remember. He was quite tall. He was dressed like a military policeman, and he only said --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll go -- we'll come to that later. Can I take it that there were four or five buses, and then a bit later some more buses arrived so that there were about ten buses in all?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I shall now try to go back to this part. You mentioned this today and you also referred to this in the statement you gave, namely I'm speaking about the statement you gave in Banja Luka. The question of Mr. McCloskey was: "Who was on those buses?" And you said: "There were women and men on the buses." Mr. McCloskey then told you: "No one so far has testified that there have been any women on those buses." Today you repeated that there were women, and you also added that there had also been children on the buses. Please try to remember: Were there on those buses women, children, and men, or were there only men on the buses?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- where I was -- the buses that I was escorting, there were men as well as the elderly and children and women.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have a number of testimonies here, Mr. Zaric, to the effect that buses with children and women were directed, as you described, from Konjevic Polje towards Kasaba, Glasinica [as interpreted], Tisce and on towards Kladanj. Is it possible, given your position as a suspect and the problem you are confronted with in terms of your memory, that you have actually mixed this up, that this was the bus that was going in the direction of Tisca, with men and women and children and elderly men, and not towards this place, not towards Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible, because really ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zaric. Because in a way this corresponds to what has been heard before this Court so far. There have been no testimonies, at least not to my knowledge, that there were women and children and the elderly taken in the direction of Zvornik. But let us try to confirm this through the questions which will follow. You said that you left them in front of the command building, that you believe was the command of the Zvornik Brigade. Do you know at all where the command of the Zvornik Brigade is?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the Zvornik Brigade was at the Standard building. Now it's the Faculty of Technology.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where this building is located, the Standard building, in what part of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards the crossing at the border with Serbia and Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this building by the main road or does one have to take a turn from the main road in order to reach the Standard facility?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One has to get off the main road, perhaps 5 metres off it in order to get into the facility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was a testimony provided here and material evidence to the effect that in the command there was a bus - when I say "the command" I mean the closed compound of the Zvornik Brigade - there was a bus there. I wanted to ask you in view of the fact that you said a while ago that the buses were held up in front of the command of the Zvornik Brigade. Can you tell us if we show you a map, can you try and indicate on the map exactly where those buses were standing?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will use the exhibit for identification marked D62, which we have provided to the Prosecution, and may I ask you also to provide one to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please kindly seek to concentrate and organise yourself and to focus on this plan, this outline of the approach, access to the facility, and try to indicate for us where were the buses standing in the command of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here in front is the road leading from Zvornik to Karakaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe that you should turn around the map, because you're pointing at the bank re -- it is -- so under -- below that in the right angle is the direction towards Zvornik and the left corner, direction Karakaj. If you can take a look at that.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please try and concentrate and we'll try to have you tell us where was it that these buses were held up in front of the command of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the gate post here. I believe that it was somewhere around this place that a truck was parked. And as far as I can recall, there was one here that was heading towards the entrance. The next bus was here where I was, the one where I was. I cannot remember exactly whether it was -- whether there was another one here around the entrance, around the gate post, another bus.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic, could we ask the witness to mark on this map the locations where the bus was?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. That would have been my next question and we would then also submit that as an exhibit of the Defence, because we will show in further proceedings that the places that he's talking about could not objectively receive all these buses. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I can ask you, please, use a pencil to mark, Mr. Zaric, mark number 1 for our benefit and circle that marked number. And make a larger circle, of course. By all means. Number 2 would be the second bus as indicated and marked by you. Please also circle that number. Were both buses entering or were here at this lay-by on the right side. Please mark that as well.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just showed us a while ago here at the entrance on the right --

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where the 2 is?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You try, you try, you try to indicate the exact is spot. You try to tell us whether there was any bus within the compound or were they in front of the compound and mark them accordingly in circles, encircle them.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one that I was escorting was around here, around this place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you mark it by 3, mark it by 3, thank you, and please also make it bolder, the line.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, I cannot recall with precision really whether it was somewhere here around this storehouse, warehouse, this bus -- I really cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I right if I say that from what you have indicated, you can only confirm that one bus was certainly -- had certainly entered the compound of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And the other one had just set off and it was stopped and this soldier came up to the driver, most probably they knew each other, and then they saw -- they talked about what was going to be done next.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you just show us on this map and also indicate the coming buses that you referred to, the buses that were coming -- which direction were they coming and where did they stop at the particular moments?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were coming from the direction of Zvornik. This is where they were. So this is -- some of them were here in front towards Karakaj. Who was escorting them is something I don't know, nor was I -- I just managed to come to this point to see what was being planned on. As this person said that the possibility existed for the buses to be emptied, to take men to Baljkovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please mark this. Can I ask you, mark this by numbers on the left margin, the coming numbers, the subsequent numbers, 4, 5, 6, namely the places from which they continued their journeys towards Karakaj.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, one was here, one here, two here, and the same applies to the rest, because they kept coming.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please put the numbers 4 and 5 there.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right if I say that the left side of this main road is a lay-by where there is enough space for buses to stop on the left side of the main --

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards Karakaj?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was the parking spot of this Standard factory and of the textile plant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, should I try to wrap up this particular question. What were people saying, then? Where were these prisoners going, the women, the children, the men, that you talked about?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This soldier who walked up to the driver only said that much. Later this person came and said, There are no problems. My people will come; they will take over the buses. And you -- if any vehicles should come along, and there should be one coming along to Drinjaca, you try to get a ride to your units. Not five minutes had passed after that. This vehicle indeed arrived. I cannot remember this moment what it looked like -- what the driver looked like. It was some sort of a passenger car. And so I sat with him and I got a ride to Drinjaca.
