utterances.text: Thank you very much. And I hope you could furnish with us and the other party for the witnesses when we resume next year, the witness list. Yes, Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm really sorry, I won't hold up the staff any longer. But I just wanted to say I will not be appearing in the case any longer. I wanted to thank this wonderful Trial Chamber. I think you're fair, astute, and the best Trial Chamber I've ever been before. My client, Mr. Jokic, for having faith in me; Mr. Stojanovic, and everybody else. And I -- it's been just an honour to be a part of history in the making and I appreciate being here. The Prosecution has been a delight to work with also. And all of the Registry, I just wanted to wish you all a Happy New Year and a Merry Christmas, and thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much. I must say that we are sorry to see you leaving this case and everybody working in the Tribunal, their work should be recognised. We appreciate your assistance and contribution to this Tribunal, especially to this case. I believe we will miss you, and sometimes your timely intervention and submissions are very helpful, at least to keep our eyes wide open. And I wish you a Merry Christmas and bright future when you come back to your State. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I think there is a housekeeping matter that we have received submission from the Prosecution about Mr. -- I think three witness statements they are filing in accordance with 92 bis. We haven't received any response from the Defence. So could I hear from the Defence whether there's any objections to the three witnesses which are Erdemovic, Deronjic, and another person.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, if I could very briefly. I'll start with Mr. Erdemovic. I don't know if you are aware but there is a stack of documents with respect to his previous statements. He has given lots of statements and he's testified on several occasions. Initially my inclination was that we would need him here to testify in light of the language which is in the Prosecution's motion, which is that he did not positively identify Bratunac Brigade soldiers. I think we can all agree that he never does and that we had an admission as well from Mr. Butler to that effect. Before committing myself, I would prefer having the Prosecutor direct me somewhat within -- to what exactly they intend to offer Mr. Erdemovic for. Is it all of his statements or is there a particular segment that they are planning on making reference to in their final argument or their case in-chief. Otherwise, I need to read the entire -- all of those statements to see if there might be something in there that they could possibly use. And so I don't want to concede at this point, but perhaps I can get together with Mr. McCloskey and talk about this and reach some sort of an agreement. Other than that, I will need some time to read all those documents carefully again, and I must confess I have not read his statement or his testimony from the Milosevic case, because we were somewhat busy with other matters. With respect to Deronjic, as I understand, as long as Mr. Deronjic is going to be here to be cross-examined, we have no objections to his prior statements and testimony coming in. So I think we can reach an agreement on that. With respect to the other witness, it would be my inclination, Your Honour, in light of what this witness will be testifying to, that we also be afforded the opportunity to cross-examine. I do not anticipate a lengthy cross-examination, but nonetheless I believe that a cross-examination will be required. And I understand he's been cross-examined by others; however, I would rather try my case and do my cross-examination, consistent with our theory of the case. So that's our position. So if I can find some flexibility with Mr. McCloskey, perhaps we can -- we will not need to have Mr. Erdemovic come forward. Because if he does, it will be a lengthy cross-examination in all likelihood, and perhaps not necessarily -- not necessary in the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, to save time, I'll turn to Mr. Stojanovic first.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have to say that for the last five years I've followed everything that Mr. Erdemovic has said, so that after I joined this case I got a different impression about all the testimonies because he was also a citizen of the same town as myself. Erdemovic or Deronjic or the third witness have nothing that touches upon our defence, except for one sentence which is mentioned in Erdemovic's testimony, referring to the expected arrival of certain construction machinery or equipment. As far as our defence is concerned, we would have no problems that all three of these statements be admitted under 92 bis, and we think that at this point we don't believe that we would have any questions for any of these witnesses. In view of, also, what Deronjic stated in his interviews and while declaring his guilty plea -- and I also had the opportunity to read back his testimony in the Milosevic and Nikolic case. So as far as I believe, I don't think that we will need to cross-examine any of those three witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation. Mr. McCloskey, can you give a very brief response to the requests?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Regarding Erdemovic, Mr. Karnavas and I have had a chance to speak briefly. I think we can work this out. Mr. Erdemovic's story has always been the same, and he -- and I can tell Mr. Karnavas and the Court that he doesn't -- he never suggests that the men that took part in the executions are from the Bratunac Brigade. He always says that he believes they're from Bratunac, based on what they've said. So that was, I think, Mr. Karnavas's main concern that we've had a chance to speak about. Otherwise, his statements are pretty much the same on -- in his telling of the story. And we can continue to talk about that and see if there's any other issues. Of course it would be best if he had a chance to read this. Regarding Deronjic, he'll be here and we'll have the chance -- everyone will have a chance to talk with him. And the other person is a Bosnian, I think she's a psychologist who has testified at length about the victim impact and the impact on the Muslim community of women. And she also has come up and testified, I believe, in another hearing here. And it would be difficult for her to come back. I know that, having been involved in that. And really, this should be what 92 bis is about. But we would stand by our motion for that witness. And the others I think we should be able to work out, no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Could we make a decision now that we admit those three statements into the evidence through the 92 bis. And we leave the opportunity for the parties to discuss whether there's any need from the Defence side to cross-examine those witnesses. It is so decided. And another matter is another witness, W-131, after examining the statement and submissions from the parties we decided the statement of this witness is admitted into the evidence under 92 bis without cross-examination. It is so decided. And we will resume on the 15th of January next year. Yes, Mr. Blagojevic. THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would just like to turn your attention to my position. I do not wish to be understood here as an object in the most elementary sense without any feelings, without personality, without character, without dignity, without anything. So please, would you consider me as an alive person who is interested in his own situation and his own fate, and a little bit broader than that. Therefore, I do not agree that certain persons can, based on their personal conclusions without any elementary or minimal contact with me, state here questions and discussions about things that have to do with my fate and the fate of my family. That gentleman has placed my fate and the fate of my family out in the clear -- out in the clear, in the field, and we -- he believes now that he can manipulate us the way he wants to. And I believe this cannot stand. As far as this first person is concerned, Erdemovic, he says, well, we have agreed with the Prosecutor. I do not accept that. The Prosecutor states that Erdemovic said that he never said that these were people from the Bratunac Brigade. I said that he did. In one statement that I read, it states that under the pressure of the investigator who was questioning him, he did say clearly that they were people from the Bratunac Brigade. These are falsities because of which I can end up in the manner that I am prepared to finish up, as if I did commit such things. But if not, the gentleman in question cannot hold that in his hands and he cannot manipulate my fate the way he believes he can. I am a little more important than he thinks I am. So please, this indicates the total futility of all of this and everything that is hanging over my head. And I am saying, I am not somebody that you can underestimate. I am not somebody that can be written off in advance, who can be spat on and rejected and put in the garbage. I believe that my dignity, and this will be proved in the end that this is so. I am prepared to bear full responsibility, and this is why I wish for this comfortable, free, irresponsible, fundamentally ill-natured acts towards my personality should stop. And I am please asking for you to protect me. I do not wish to take up any more of your time, and I thank you for listening to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Blagojevic, I think the position of the Bench is very clear. And your submissions are registered in the transcript already. We believe that this Bench fully respected your legitimate right in this trial. And we have to do whatever we could to help you to help yourself. We quite understand the situation you are in at this moment, and we will entrust the Defence counsel, Mr. Karnavas, during the break to try his best to approach Mr. Blagojevic and to talk those matters over. And we demand Mr. Karnavas to send us a report in the situation. And we also entrust the Registrar to send a legal officer to discuss with Mr. Blagojevic to understand his situation and to try to help him to follow the instructions this Bench made in our decisions. You may sit down, please. THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just one more question, because of this report that you have ordered. I would also like this report to include how far the investigations have gone in the criminal act of cheating for which I am accused of. This is a new charge that I have to bring out here, the act of falsehood, of cheating. This is clear in the decision of the Appeals Chamber. I think this is paragraph 46.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. We will look to it, but frankly speaking, this is the first time for me to hear about this. I promise you that we will look into it. THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Unfortunately that's what it states.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may sit down, please. THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think this Bench is very grateful to the interpreters and the technicians working inside this courtroom and outside this courtroom. It's 20 minutes past the limits, and I wish all the persons involved in this case and Mr. Blagojevic and Mr. Jokic a Merry Christmas and a Happy New Year. And we'll resume on January 15th of next year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: at 7.18 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 15th day of January, 2003 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
